Recommended: Yes (Base Game) / DLC: Optional

"A thrilling Souls roguelike loop, but chaotic timers and brutal RNG demand frequent breaks."

With just shy of 200 hours logged alongside my co-op partner, I can say Nightreign offers a genuinely exciting, high-stakes spin on the Elden Ring formula. The transition into a roguelike structure brings a lot to like right out of the gate: built-in cooperative play without hoops to jump through, an intuitive button layout, zero fall damage for high-mobility traversal, and that unmistakable, exhilarating rush when you finally topple a brutal boss.

However, the frustrations here hit very differently than they do in standard Elden Ring. In the mainline game, hitting a wall rarely kills your momentum—you can always explore elsewhere, level up, and feel continuous progression. In Nightreign, the combination of harsh timers and wild RNG can make a bad run feel intensely discouraging rather than rewarding.

What Works

Smooth Co-op & Mechanics: The built-in multiplayer makes tackling runs with a dedicated partner seamless (and spares you from rolling the dice on random matchmaking). The controls feel tight, and removing fall damage lets traversal stay fast-paced and fluid.

The Boss Rush High: Overcoming the initial slate of bosses through coordinated team play delivers that peak FromSoftware satisfaction.

Addictive Run Variety: When the loot RNG aligns and your builds click, hunting down targets across the shifting landscape is a blast.

What Frustrates

Brutal RNG Meets Strict Timers: When drop luck goes south while a countdown forces your hand, the resulting pressure shifts from fun tension to outright demoralization. Losing a run simply because the loot refused to cooperate stings a lot more than a standard death in Elden Ring.

Map & Loot Segregation in the DLC: Separating the expansion locations and gear pools from the base map feels counterintuitive for a roguelike that thrives on variety and synergy.

Steep Wall for Added Bosses: While we conquered the base game bosses, the expansion's added encounters are tuned to an extreme level. They currently feel out of reach without near-flawless RNG, leading to long breaks away from the game rather than the eager "one more run" feeling of earlier hours.

Final Verdict:
Nightreign is an easy recommendation for fans of tactical co-op and roguelike runs who want fast-paced, high-stakes combat. The base game is deeply satisfying to clear, but be prepared for heavy RNG fatigue. The DLC is fun if you want an extreme challenge, but it is entirely optional to get full value out of the game.

Something tells me this one was forced upon FromSoftware, kind of like how Marathon and Anthem were forced on Bungie and BioWare.

But it seems like the team still managed to make it unique in some way. The characters are cool, and the new bosses are sick.

Still, it really makes me think: what if this had just been DLC for the base Elden Ring? Or a separate game series? Or hell, what if they'd worked on it more and turned it into a full-fledged Elden Ring 2?

Awful experience for someone new to the game. You will feel basically useless as you hope someone has a clue where to go, and what route to take. If you try to pick where to go, someone else will decide to go to another spot. Knowing where to go, and the proper route basically decides if you are going to win or not, since you won't be nearly as powerful as you should be, and you will be less familiar with the bosses as a new player. Figuring that route on your own is nigh impossible given the time limit. You will basically have to learn from other people, and hope you can actually keep up.
Identification of where teammates are is really difficult. The compass isn't enough, and if your teammate is close by, but above or beneath you, it's difficult to tell where they are, without looking all over the place. It would be nice if there was an icon on the edge of the screen to help point out where they are, when they go running off ahead, thinking they are leading, but leaving everyone else behind instead. The name above their character isn't enough for this type of game.

Since it's geared towards co-op play, it will be difficult to learn what you are doing because you cannot respawn and replay the boss. You have to go through the whole run and then get another try. I pretty much felt like a burden.

I consistently never get anything geared to my character. I'll play duchess and end up with a colossal sword in each hand.

The vertical traversal feels awful. The constant button mashing to jump up tombstones feels ridiculous, like this is some mario platformer. One of the most frustrating parts of this game is missing some jump, and falling a massive distance that basically makes you useless to your teammates as you try to find a way to where they are.

I feel like this game requires you to study videos to have a chance of being competent. Either that or you have some friend show you through it.

Not really enjoying it as much as Elden Ring. I'll play it more I'm sure, but I wish there was an easier entry for people trying to learn how it works, and how to route properly.

How big is the gap between Depth 4 and Depth 5?

In my personal experience, the main difficulty of Depth 4 lies in the Night King battle. As early as Depth 3, players have figured out how to farm by fighting Sinners. Unless you mess up extremely badly in the early game, you can almost always get through the opening phase. However, starting from Depth 4, squishy classes can no longer tank certain moves from the Night King—sometimes you still die even with full damage reduction stacked.

By the time you reach Depth 5, most players have fought the Night King enough times. Apart from the Ice Dragon and the Fairy boss, it’s really hard to wipe on the other fights. The only thing I fear about the Ice Dragon is the unmarked ground spikes—the ones that only pop up right under your feet the very second they’re about to hit. The other nightmare scenario is just bad RNG: no good damage-related relics, and your teammates are playing classes like Snail or Hermit that can’t interrupt the big cast. Once the Ice Dragon gets its second ultimate off, it’s basically a slow, guaranteed wipe.

Some people say Depth 5 feels no different from Depth 4. If you’re playing squishy classes like Hermit or Snail, you still die from one single hit either way. The only real difference is that Depth 5 drops way better relics. After all, a truly skilled player can clear Depth 5 even without any relics at all—it just takes a lot longer because of the lack of damage.

I loved Elden Ring so I bought this game. It is fun at first, the initial standard boss fights are all possible without really having to worry about relics. There's a character for each playstyle and you can further customize them with said relic effects. However once you beat the standard bosses and get into deep of the night as well as the ever-dark variants relics become absolutely necessary. If you don't enjoy grinding you likely won't get really good effects for your relics. As far as I can tell no additional bosses or items are coming to the game anytime soon and that leaves a-lot to be desired in terms of adding things from the other souls games. Overall, Solid game would recommend to pick up with a friend on sale.
